title: SQL Injection in DB-API via f-string Formatting
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x with any PEP 249 DB-API driver (sqlite3, psycopg, mysqlclient, etc.)
security_mechanism: PEP 249 defines parameter binding (placeholder + params), but Python string formatting (f-string, %, .format, +) composes the SQL text before the driver parses it, so a value containing a quote or SQL syntax is read as statement structure, not data. Parameter binding sends values out-of-band so they can never change the parse; format strings can also smuggle multi-statement payloads where the driver permits them.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters, JSON fields, sort/filter names from the client that are interpolated into the statement text.
source_sink_clues.sink: cursor.execute / cursor.executemany / connection cursor text built with f-string, %, .format, or concatenation

tracking_guards: Verify execute is called with two arguments (sql with placeholder, params sequence) rather than one pre-formatted string; for identifiers that cannot be parameterized (table/column names, ORDER BY direction) require an allowlist dictionary mapping client keys to fixed SQL fragments.
not_candidate_when: Values are bound through the driver's parameter mechanism, or the only interpolated parts come from a fixed server-side allowlist (never from raw client text).
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
PEP 249: Python Database API Specification (parameter binding) — https://peps.python.org/pep-0249/
OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
